Nano-metal diborides are prepared by a novel disulphide-to-diboride transition route, in which the entropy contribution to the Gibbs free energy by generation of gaseous sulfur-containing products plays a crucial role. The nano-metal diborides,$\mathsf{T a B}_{2}$ in particular, are investigated as the support of $\mathrm{IrO}_{2}$ nanocatalysts, which finally forms a $\mathrm{TaO_{x}/IrO_{2}}$ heterojunction catalytic layer on $\mathrm{TaB}_{2}$ : surface. Multiple advantageous properties are achieved simultaneously by the resulting composite material (denoted as $\mathrm{IrO_{2}@TaB_{2}}$ 1,including high electrical conductivity, improved iridium mass activity and enhanced corrosion resistance. As a consequence, the $\mathrm{IrO_{2}@TaB_{2}}$ : can be used to fabricate the membrane electrode with a low iridium loading of $0.15\mathrm{m g}\mathrm{c m}^{-2}$ ,and to give an excellent catalytic performance (3.06 A cm2@2.0 V@80 C) in PEMWE—the one that is usually inaccessible by unsupported Ir-based nanocatalysts and the vast majority of existing supported Ir-based catalysts at such a low iridium loading. Herein, we present the entropy-driven synthesis of high-surfacearea nano-metal diboride from the corresponding disulphide, and demonstrate the practical usefulness of boride ceramics, especially $\mathtt{T a B}_{2},$ _, as the effective support material of anode nanocatalyst $\mathrm{I r O}_{2}$ in PEMWE. The $\mathsf{T a B_{2}}\mathtt{-s u p p o r t e d}$ $\mathrm{I r O}_{2}$ !nanocatalyst (denoted as $\mathrm{IrO_{2}@TaB_{2}}$ 'possesses a large electrical conductivity $(0.1–0.2\;\mathrm{S}\;\mathrm{c m}^{-1})$ !similar to nano·,$\mathbf{\cdot}\mathbf{\mathsf{I r O}}_{2}$ itself, shows about 10 times higher iridium mass activity than $\mathrm{IrO_{2}}$ ,and exhibits much lower iridium leaching than $\mathrm{IrO}_{2}$ during electrocatalysis. When integrated into a PEM single-cell electrolyzer, the $\mathrm{IrO_{2}@TaB_{2}}$ :can achieve $3.06\mathrm{A}\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$ current density at 2.0Vand 80C(membrane: NafionN15),with a low iridium-loading of 0.15 mg cm-. The performance of our PEMWE has reached that of US DOE 2023 target $(1.9V@2.5A cm^{-2}$ , platinum group metal (PGM)loading of1mg cm-2), under a much lowr PGM loading $(0.15\mathrm{m g}_{\mathrm{i r}}\mathrm{c m}^{-2}$ and $0.27mg_{Pt}cm^{-2}$ ).

We further compare the performance of PEMWEs using $\mathrm{IrO_{2}@TaB_{2}}$ and commercial $\mathrm{I r O}_{2}$ as anode electrocatalysts (Fig. 5c),under the similar Ir loading in CCM. While $\mathsf{I r O}_{2}$ employing as anode layer, the PEMWE delivers a significantly lower current density of $1.9\mathrm{A}\mathrm{c m}^{-2}$ relative to $\mathrm{IrO_{2}@TaB_{2}}$ :catalyst $(3.06\mathrm{A}\mathrm{c m}^{-2})$ at 2.0Vcell potential. To evaluate catalyst stability, the $\mathrm{I r O}_{2}$ and IrO₂@TaB2 anode cells were tested at a constant current density of 1$1\mathrm{A}\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$ The PEMWE using $\mathrm{I r O}_{2}$ anode undergoes a severe deactivation under the low Ir loading of $0.2\mathrm{m g}\mathrm{c m}^{-2}$ , and the $\mathrm{I r O_{2}}$ anode cell exhibits reasonable stability when the Ir loading increases to 2mg $\mathrm{cm^{-2}}$ (Fig. 5e and Supplementary Fig.21-24).By comparison, the PEMWE using $\mathrm{IrO_{2}@TaB_{2}}$ 1anode provides a steady operation for more than 120 h under a low Ir loading of 0.15 mgcm2(Fig.5e),confirming excellentcatalytic stability. We can speculate that the $\mathrm{IrO_{2}@TaB_{2}}$  with larger material volume can forms a thicker catalyst layer relative to bare $\mathrm{I r O}_{2},$ ,so that the former possesses sufficient layer conductivity and stability at such a low Ir loading. The great activity and stability demonstrate the great potential of $\mathrm{IrO_{2}@TaB_{2}}$ as a practical anode of real PEMwE for commercial application.

We further characterized the $\mathsf{T a B}_{2}$ sample with SEM and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). The SEM (Supplementary Fig. 2f)and TEM images (Fig. le) present hat $\mathsf{T a B}_{2}$ nanosheets possess an edge length of 200-500 nm and a thickness of 5-20 nm. High-resolution TEM image (HRTEM)of $\mathtt{T a B}_{2}$ nanosheet (Fig. lf)  reveals its good crystallinity. In the HRTEM image and the corresponding selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern (Fig.1f, inset), interplanar spacing of 0.268nm could be observed for three sets of lattice fringes,assigning to {001} planes of $\mathsf{T a B}_{2}$ phase. The angle of 60 between the three planes is consistent with the theoretical value. Moreover,$\mathsf{N}_{2}$ c adsorption-desorption isotherms of $\mathsf{T a B_{2}}$ 2display typical type-Il curves with H3 hysteresis loop (Fig. 1d), suggesting the presence of interlaminar pores among adjacent nanosheets. The BET surface area of TaB2 is calculated to be $54.6\mathrm{m}^{2}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ 1.These results demonstrate the successful synthesis of high-quality $\mathsf{T a B}_{2}$ :nanosheet with large surface areas.
